doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Jacobs's first day at Decca and the missing trumpet part
summary: As a Decca secretary she placed lead sheets for Armstrong, found no trumpet part, and learned nobody writes parts for Louis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No. No. All you had to do was play it for Louis. No in fact you know when I first met Louis I worked at Decca Records. I know poor Jackie’s heard the story ten times. But the first day I was there Milt Gabler and Sy Oliver, who was his musical director and Milt Gabler was the A&R man, who incidentally is Billy Crystal’s uncle, darling man, wonderful, I loved him. They employed me as a secretary, sharpen pencils, file, you know all kind of that really coolie jobs. But they gave me the music and told me to bring it out to the recording studio. So I put the lead sheets on all the music stands and then I came to the music stands in front of the microphone which was Louis’ microphone and I didn’t have a trumpet part. So I went back in the office and I was absolutely beside myself. I started to cry. I thought well I’m losing my job. So everybody got hysterical laughing and when Louis came they told him, you see this girl? She lost your music. Well for years he never let me forget it. And of course what the funny part was that they told me that nobody writes a part for Louis. He just hears the song and he wings it.
